meanings: verb: to invite or attract to come to
examples: Julie was supposed to spend all day in the library, but the sun beckoned as she passed a window and she couldn't resist going outside.

meanings: adjective: unable to do well, bad at
examples: In spite of his strong resume, it quickly became clear that the new analyst was inept, incapable of performing the most basic analyses.

meanings: adjective: originating in a certain area
examples: Many think the potato is indigenous to Europe, but it actually originated in what is now Peru.

meanings: verb: to enlarge or increase; to improve
examples: General Lee's army was augmented when Jackson joined to add his 17,000 men in support of Lee's goals.

meanings: adjective: perfectly appropriate
examples: The lion is sometimes called "king of the beasts," an apt description given the animal's appearance and power.

meanings: noun: a serious disease that kills many people
examples: Sarah wept as she told her children the story of the plague that had killed her village, leaving only two survivors to continue their traditions.

meanings: verb: to grow stronger or healthier
examples: A good gardener knows plants flourish only with the right amount of sun and water.

meanings: verb: to be slowly destroyed by wind and rain
examples: The Appalachian mountains are lower than the young Rocky Mountains because the Appalachians have been steadily eroding for much longer.

meanings: adjective: produced or growing in very large numbers
examples: The presidential candidate’s campaign became one of the most popular in history, with a profuse number of supporters attending each of his speeches.

meanings: noun: a short period of calm or inactivity
examples: Once Mark and Petra finally got their screaming baby to sleep, they sat quietly, afraid that even a whisper would break the first lull in three days.

meanings: adjective: confident, sophisticated, and polite
examples: The waiter was so urbane that he maintained his professionalism even when the customer began explaining the unpleasant details of her surgery.

meanings: verb: to stop somebody's plan
examples: Aeroman, the inexperienced town superhero, failed to thwart the villain’s plans to take over the city, which was soon renamed Villiantown.

meanings: adjective: extremely small
examples: The introduction of the electron microscope made it possible to view infinitesimally small details on cells.

meanings: adjective: called a something that is not appropriate (used before the incorrect term)
examples: "I can't believe that I thought William was really an Olympic athlete!" Helen fumed. "That so-called gold medal was made from chocolate and tin foil!"

meanings: adjective: not caring about hurting people
examples: The ruthless leader ordered bombings of the southern border of his own country, where thousands of his people lived, in order to win the battle.

meanings: noun: hate and conflict
examples: Jan had fought loudly with her mother every day until she left for college, so the rest of the family enjoyed the break from the strife.

meanings: verb: to change shape; to become something new
examples: I am amazed by his ability to morph a shapeless lump of clay into a delicate and perfectly symmetrical vase.

meanings: adjective: well known and respected
examples: Although the poet was not appreciated or recognized during his lifetime, he became widely celebrated for his creativity after his death.

meanings: verb: to collect together slowly over time into a larger amount
examples: Billy stored his favorite old toys in his parents' basement, where dust and spider webs slowly accreted on the forgotten plastic soldiers and trucks.

meanings: adjective: impossible to deny or disprove
examples: Though highly controversial centuries ago, the idea that the Earth goes around the Sun is now irrefutable.

meanings: adjective: more than is needed; very fancy
examples: Fido's birthday feast was lavish; most guests thought that a dog would not be able to appreciate the bits of gold in his steak-flavored ice cream.

meanings: verb: to spin or turn around
examples: Lily's chair squeaked when it rotated, which drove her coworkers crazy due to her habit of swiveling while thinking.

meanings: noun: a small difference in meaning or a very small detail
examples: Listen to your favorite song on these $500 headphones and you'll hear nuances you'd never heard before.

meanings: noun: something very popular for a short time
examples: Doctors spent several months raising public awareness about the negative effects of the new diet craze that was sweeping the country.

meanings: verb: to decide not to use or have something good
examples: Terry had to forgo his summer backpacking trip across Europe in order to save money to fix his car instead.

meanings: verb: cancel by being opposite but equal in amount
examples: In order to offset his father’s vote to build a new high-speed cross-country train, Larry voted against building the train.

meanings: verb: to make seem small or unimportant by comparison
examples: Jennifer was excited about her basketball team's victory, but her older brother then announced his wife's pregnancy and overshadowed her news.

meanings: noun: a cause or reason to start an action
examples: Before John met Amanda, all his shirts were old and filled with holes, but his desire to impress her gave him the impetus to buy all new clothes.

meanings: adjective: not secret or hidden
examples: The disagreement between the neighbors grew from quiet, angry looks to overt hatred as they began throwing eggs at each other's houses.

meanings: adjective: extremely sad, without hope
examples: Fariha was a very strong woman, and she never became despondent no matter how many misfortunes she went through.

meanings: noun: a false name used publicly
examples: To avoid public attention, the author decided that rather than using her real name, she would use a pseudonym when publishing her novels.

meanings: verb: to decrease in power or size
examples: The politician's career waned as the widening gap between his views and those of who he represented became more obvious.

meanings: verb: to slow the progress of or make more difficult
examples: Batgirl's high heels once again hindered her ability to chase the bank robbers; she wondered why she couldn't wear comfortable boots as Batman did.

meanings: adjective: experienced at doing something
examples: Given the managers’ extensive experience, the boss requested that each of her seasoned managers work closely with new hires.

meanings: adjective: requiring and demanding accuracy
examples: Though his childhood piano teacher was so exacting, Max is thankful now, having become a professional pianist.

meanings: verb: to create (something strong) through a large effort
examples: Climate change cannot be fixed by any one government; if we are going to stop it, nations around the world must forge a partnership.

meanings: adjective: many in number or very common (used for bad things)
examples: Never believe anything you hear in a politician's speech; they are rife with inaccuracies and even lies.

meanings: verb: to come together for a formal discussion or meeting
examples: In response to the school's poor performance on tests, the principal and his best teachers convened to improve the curriculum.

meanings: adjective: hard but easy to break
examples: Unaware that the tree was diseased, the boy had no idea that the thick branch he was climbing on was actually brittle and ready to snap.

meanings: noun: a class that students can select from among alternatives
examples: While some classes are mandatory for all biology students, others such as parasitology and botany are electives.

meanings: verb: to cover completely with liquid
examples: We regretted not checking the weather before leaving home when we were quickly drenched by an unexpected summer storm.

meanings: verb: to remove by digging in the ground
examples: The new apartment building will have underground parking, so the entire site is being excavated, after which they'll build up from the lowest level.

meanings: verb: to slow the progress of or make more difficult
examples: The steep incline and hot weather hampered the group's efforts to reach the top of the hill in time to see the fireworks.

meanings: verb: to completely confuse
examples: The overly technical vocabulary of the paper baffled the students who did not have as much experience as their older classmates.

meanings: verb: increase or improve after a low point
examples: Even after his investors and customers had abandoned him, Charles still thought his xylophone business was going to make a rebound.

meanings: adjective: very noticeable
examples: The fact that oil companies have shown a marked interest in the lawmaker's proposition should generate some suspicion.

meanings: verb: to officially end a bad system
examples: The candidate for student president promised to abolish homework, grades and exams; unfortunately, she lost because nobody believed it was possible.

meanings: adjective: giving careful attention to detail
examples: The surgeon's fastidious attention to each and every tiny cut or stitch frustrated his staff but overjoyed his patients.

meanings: verb: to live somewhere
examples: Creatures that dwell deep in the darkest caves have lost all color in their skin and become blind from the darkness.

meanings: adjective: unimportant and small
examples: Even though most would consider it a trivial problem, Mr. Sheldon spent an hour in the meeting questioning where his favorite pen had disappeared to.
